indicator.subject: Science
indicator.content_standard: B2.3.1.1: Recognize that different parts of the human body work independently to perform a specific function
indicator.objective: Know the functions of the human body parts such as eyes, ears, mouth, nose, arms, legs and hands

skills.description: State the function of specific body parts
Match a body part to its function or identify the part used for a specific action
Explain simply what happens if a body part is missing or not working well
Draw and colour at least two body parts

misconceptions: The nose is only for breathing; it has nothing to do with smelling.
Hands are only for holding; they cannot feel.
If one part is missing, the person cannot do anything at all.
Ears are for seeing and eyes are for hearing.
The mouth is only for eating; it is not for talking.

questions.stem: Which body part do we use to see things around us?
questions.explanation: We use our eyes to see the world around us.
questions.misconception: Pupils may confuse eyes with ears.

questions.stem: Which body part do we use to hear sounds?
hints: It is on the side of your head.
questions.explanation: We use our ears to hear sounds.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think we hear with our eyes.

questions.stem: What do we use our nose for?
hints: You use it to sniff food.
It is in the middle of your face.
questions.explanation: We use our nose to smell things.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think the nose is only for breathing.

questions.stem: Which body parts do we use to walk and run?
questions.explanation: We use our legs to walk and run.
questions.misconception: Pupils may confuse legs with arms.

questions.stem: Kofi wants to pick up a pencil. Which body part will he use?
hints: You use it to hold things.
questions.explanation: We use our hands to pick up and hold objects.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think legs are used for picking up things.

questions.stem: What is the main function of the mouth?
questions.explanation: The mouth is used for eating, drinking, and speaking.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think the mouth is only for eating, not speaking.

questions.stem: Ama is listening to music. Which part of her body is she using?
questions.explanation: Ama uses her ears to listen to music.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think you listen with your eyes.

questions.stem: What do we use our hands for?
hints: You use them to catch a ball.
questions.explanation: We use our hands to hold, touch, write, and do many tasks.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think hands are only for holding.

questions.stem: What happens if a person's eyes are not working well?
hints: If they don't work, seeing is hard.
questions.explanation: If a person's eyes are not working well, they cannot see clearly or at all.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think a person who cannot see also cannot hear.

questions.stem: Which body part do we use to kick a football?
hints: It is the lower part of your body.
questions.explanation: We use our legs and feet to kick a football.
questions.misconception: Pupils may say hands because they throw balls.

questions.stem: Name the body part we use to smell food.
hints: It is in the middle of your face.
questions.explanation: We use the nose to smell food.

questions.stem: What do we use our ears for?
hints: You listen to music with them.
questions.explanation: We use our ears for hearing.

questions.stem: If a person is deaf, which body part is not working well?
questions.explanation: If a person is deaf, their ears are not working well, and they cannot hear.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think deafness affects the eyes.

questions.stem: Kwame is carrying a heavy bucket. Which two body parts is he using most?
hints: He holds the bucket with one part.
questions.explanation: Kwame uses his hands to carry the bucket and his legs to walk.
questions.misconception: Pupils may not connect the action to the correct body parts.

questions.stem: Why is it important to take care of our body parts?
options: So they can work well and we stay healthy
hints: You want your body to work.
questions.explanation: We take care of our body parts so they keep working well and we stay healthy.
questions.misconception: Pupils may not see the link between care and function.

questions.stem: Ama is blind. Which body part is not working well?
questions.explanation: A blind person's eyes are not working well, so they cannot see.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think blindness affects the ears.

questions.stem: Draw a human head and label the eyes, ears, nose, and mouth.
hints: Draw a circle for the head.
Put the eyes, nose, and mouth in the middle.
questions.explanation: This tests identifying and labelling the main parts of the face.

questions.stem: Explain how your life would change if you could not use your hands for one day.

criteria.description: States a valid difficulty (e.g., cannot write, cannot eat)

hints: What do you do with your hands every day?
How would you hold a pencil?
questions.explanation: Without hands, everyday tasks like writing, eating, and dressing would be very difficult.

questions.stem: Tell your teacher the function of the eyes, ears, nose, and mouth.
hints: What do you do with each one?
questions.explanation: This tests verbal recall of body part functions.

questions.stem: Draw a person and draw arrows pointing to the hands and legs. Write what each part does.

criteria.description: Draws a person with hands and legs
Writes a correct function for the hands
Writes a correct function for the legs

hints: Use your drawing to show how you hold and walk.
questions.explanation: This tests the connection between body parts and their functions.
